text:
Alex Ryan: Quick Q — I accidentally bought a single conference registration that included an optional pre-workshop (hands-on, job-related) plus a spouse dinner add-on. One charge on my card for $540 (merchant showed one total receipt, no breakdown). Workshop ~ $400, spouse dinner ~$140. Can I expense both? If not, what's the cleanest way to submit — traveling next week so need quick guidance.

Paula (People Ops): Workshop is reimbursable if it's job-related and your manager signs off. Spouse dinner is personal unless pre-approved as a recruiting/partner event.

Sam (Finance): Agree with Paula. We need an itemized receipt or an explicit breakdown. If merchant can't provide itemized invoice, we accept: 1) manager approval email attached in the expense, plus 2) a short attestation saying how you split the charge.

Alex Ryan: Merchant gave me a single PDF receipt with no line items. Any prefered way to show the split in the expense tool?

Paula (People Ops): Two fast flows: 1) Ask the merchant for an itemized invoice (best). 2) If they can't, get manager sign-off (reply in thread or short email) and upload your card statement + attestation explaining the split. Finance will reimburse only the business portion.

Sam (Finance): If you submit the single receipt, please enter two lines in Expensify (or Concur): business portion and personal portion. Attach the single receipt and the manager approval screenshot. We'll calculate tax/fees prorated. Example we accept: 
``
Expense lines:
- Conference workshop (business) — $400 — TAG: CONFERENCE — attach: merchant_receipt.pdf + manager_approval.pdf
- Spouse dinner (personal) — $140 — TAG: PERSONAL — attach: attestation.txt
Notes: taxes/processing fees split pro rata.
```

Marcus (Finance): Practical note: if company card was charged the full amount and we only reimburse the business portion, reimbursement goes to your personal account. If you want the merchant to refund the personal portion to the company card instead, you'll need a merchant refund (they have to issue it).

Paula (People Ops): Also: per policy, spouse/guest expenses are eligible only when pre-approved for a clear business reason (recruiting, partner-hosted event, etc.). Please include a one-line justification if you think this qualifies. For future bookings, add a comment in the booking or get prior approval to avoid the split. :thumbsup:

Alex Ryan: Thanks — I'll ask the merchant for an itemized invoice. If they can't, I'll get manager sign-off and upload the bank stmt + attestation. I'll tag expense with CONFERENCE and attach approval.

people-ops-bot: FYI — policy link: https://redwood.internal/policies/travel-expense#conference-registrations

Sam (Finance): If you want, forward the merchant PDF here and I'll take a look and suggest the exact numbers to put in the expense lines.

Alex Ryan: Sending it now — thanks everyone! :pray:
